items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The interviewee lists 'Mushiclata Hasashaion(alto sax)' as a member of the Jimmie Lunceford band, but does not describe a personal interaction or relationship with them.

ctx.x: In February we played two weeks at the Savoy, but the joint didn't send me the way it had done when I was there with the band of the Scott Brothers. Later in February, we went to Boston for a one nighter and played a battle of music with the Jimmie Lunceford band. This was really a challenge to Sy because he would have the chance of showing his ex-boss what a good band he had built in a few months time. But the honours were equally divided and both Sy and Jimmie, as well as members of the two orchestras were…

Jimmie had some musicians that had already made good names for themselves and some that were to become better known later. Those that were better known in the jazz world at the time wre Edwin Wilcox (piano) Albert Morris(Guitar) Charles Parham(bass) Earl Carruthers (baritone sax) Joe Thomas(tenor sax) Omar Simeon, a great New Orleans clarinetist and Russell Bowles(trombone). Those that were to become better known later were Joe Wilder(trumpet) Rennald Jones(trumpet) and Albert(Al)Grey(trombone). The other members…
Russell Green (trumpet) Alfred Cobb (trombone) Nick Brooks (vocalist) and Kirtland Bradford (vocalist).
